plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 21: The Second Law of Thermodynamics
plan.contextChunk: This figure sets four cylinder-and-piston drawings side by side as the successive steps of a cycle. Each cylinder holds a gray region stippled with dots for the gas, capped by a piston whose stem rises from the open top, and each stands inside a large colored block representing its surroundings. In the first, a red block labeled "Reservoir" and "(Temperature Th)" sends a thick gray arrow Qh upward into the gas while a green arrow W1 points up from the piston stem. The second sits in a pale block labeled "Insulation", green arrow W2 pointing up and the gas column taller. The third stands in a blue "Reservoir" block marked "(Temperature Tc)", with a green arrow W3 pointing down onto the piston and a gray arrow Qc leaving downward. The fourth returns to an "Insulation" block, with W4 pointing down and the gas at its shortest column. Bold captions run beneath: "Step 1: Isothermal expansion", "Step 2: Adiabatic expansion", "Step 3: Isothermal compression", and "Step 4: Adiabatic compression", each followed by a transition written M to N, N to O, O to P, and P to M. Left to right, block color, arrow direction, and gas volume shift together to track where heat crosses the boundary and which way work is done. The sequence lays out the four processes of the Carnot cycle for an ideal gas.

interactionPlan.concept: The Carnot cycle consists of four ordered reversible processes — isothermal expansion in contact with a hot reservoir, adiabatic expansion under insulation, isothermal compression against a cold reservoir, and adiabatic compression under insulation — in which heat crosses the boundary only during the two isothermal steps while work is exchanged in all four.
elements: Four cylinder-and-piston panels arranged left to right, one per step of the cycle
Panel 1 surround: large red/salmon block labeled 'Reservoir' with sub-label '(Temperature T_h)'
Panel 2 surround: pale peach block labeled 'Insulation'
Panel 3 surround: blue block labeled 'Reservoir' with sub-label '(Temperature T_c)'
Panel 4 surround: pale peach block labeled 'Insulation'
Cylinder walls: open-topped gray-outlined rectangles, one per panel
Gas column in each cylinder: light gray fill stippled with small gray dots, height varying — medium (Step 1 start), tall (Step 2), tallest at start of Step 3 shrinking, shortest (Step 4 end)
Piston in each cylinder: pale lavender/blue slab sitting on top of the gas with a narrow vertical stem rising out of the cylinder mouth
Green work arrows: W1 upward (panel 1), W2 upward (panel 2), W3 downward (panel 3), W4 downward (panel 4), each with italic subscripted label
Thick gray heat arrows: Q_h pointing upward into the gas from the hot reservoir (panel 1), Q_c pointing downward out of the gas into the cold reservoir (panel 3); no heat arrow in panels 2 and 4
Bold captions beneath each panel: 'Step 1: Isothermal expansion (M→N)', 'Step 2: Adiabatic expansion (N→O)', 'Step 3: Isothermal compression (O→P)', 'Step 4: Adiabatic compression (P→M)'
Alternate view: p–V diagram with pressure axis (vertical, label 'p') and volume axis (horizontal, label 'V')
p–V closed loop with four labeled corner points M, N, O, P
p–V curve segments: M→N shallow isotherm at T_h, N→O steeper adiabat, O→P isotherm at T_c, P→M steeper adiabat, arrowheads showing clockwise traversal
p–V annotations: dashed isotherm guide curves labeled T_h and T_c, shaded loop interior labeled 'net work W'
Legend keying green = work, gray = heat, red = hot reservoir, blue = cold reservoir, peach = insulation

interactions.label: Carnot step
interactions.teaches: The cycle is an ordered sequence: gas expands hot, expands while insulated and cools, is compressed cold, then is compressed while insulated and reheats back to the starting state.

interactions.label: Show boundary condition
interactions.teaches: Heat crosses the cylinder wall only when the gas touches a reservoir; under insulation Q = 0 and the temperature must change instead.
interactions._note: Selecting a filter dims the non-matching panels and hides their heat arrows, making the Q-in / Q-out pairing explicit.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Each physical piston picture is one leg of the closed p-V loop; the highlighted panel and the highlighted curve segment are the same process seen two ways.

demo_steps.title: Step 1 — Isothermal expansion (M→N)
demo_steps.narration: The cylinder sits on the hot reservoir at T_h. Heat Q_h flows in (gray arrow up) exactly as fast as the gas does work W1 lifting the piston, so the temperature never changes and the gas expands.

demo_steps.title: Step 2 — Adiabatic expansion (N→O)
demo_steps.narration: The cylinder is now wrapped in insulation, so no heat arrow appears. The gas keeps expanding and does work W2, but that energy can only come from its own internal energy, so it cools from T_h to T_c.

demo_steps.title: Step 3 — Isothermal compression (O→P)
demo_steps.narration: Placed on the cold reservoir at T_c, the gas is compressed: work W3 is done on it downward while heat Q_c is dumped out to the cold reservoir, holding the temperature fixed.

demo_steps.title: Step 4 — Adiabatic compression (P→M)
demo_steps.narration: Insulated again, the gas is compressed to its smallest volume by work W4 with no heat exchange, which raises its temperature back to T_h and returns it to state M.

demo_steps.title: Where heat crosses the boundary
demo_steps.narration: Filter to the thermal-contact steps only: heat enters in Step 1 and leaves in Step 3. Every other energy transfer in the cycle is work, not heat.

demo_steps.title: Insulated legs change temperature, not heat
demo_steps.narration: Now filter to the insulated steps. With Q = 0, the work done goes entirely into or out of internal energy, which is what carries the gas between T_h and T_c.

demo_steps.title: The same cycle as a p-V loop
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the p-V view: the four panels become the four legs of a closed clockwise loop M→N→O→P→M. The shallow legs are isotherms, the steep legs adiabats, and the enclosed area is the net work output.

demo_steps.title: Linking picture to path
demo_steps.narration: Side by side, stepping through the cycle highlights one cylinder and its matching curve segment together, so piston motion, heat flow, and position on the loop are read as a single process.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Heat enters only at T_h and leaves only at T_c; the two insulated legs exist purely to move the gas between those two temperatures without any heat crossing the boundary — which is why the closed loop encloses net work and why Carnot efficiency depends only on T_h and T_c.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Layout: four equal-width vertical panels in a row, each a tall colored surround block containing an open-topped gray-outlined cylinder. Surround colors left to right: saturated red (hot reservoir), pale peach (insulation), medium blue (cold reservoir), pale peach (insulation), each with its bold centered label near the bottom and reservoirs carrying an italic '(Temperature T_h)' / '(Temperature T_c)' line just below the block. Gas is a light-gray rectangle stippled with evenly scattered small dark-gray dots; the piston is a thin pale lavender slab with a narrow stem poking above the cylinder mouth. Gas column height grows across panels 1→2 (expansion) and shrinks across 3→4 (compression), shortest at the end of Step 4. Work arrows are thin green arrows beside the piston stem, pointing up in panels 1 and 2 and down in panels 3 and 4, labeled W1..W4 with italic subscripts. Heat arrows are thick gray arrows only in panels 1 (up, into gas, labeled Q_h) and 3 (down, out of gas, labeled Q_c). Bold two-line captions run beneath each panel with the step number, process name, and transition arrow (M→N etc.). Active step is shown by a bright outline / full opacity on its panel while others dim to ~35% opacity. The alternate p-V view is a clean line plot with p on the vertical axis and V on the horizontal, a clockwise closed quadrilateral-like loop with labeled corners M (upper left), N, O, P, shallow isothermal legs drawn in warm red (T_h) and cool blue (T_c), steep adiabatic legs in neutral dark gray, dashed extended isotherm guides labeled T_h and T_c, arrowheads mid-segment, and a lightly shaded interior labeled 'net work'. The highlighted segment matches the color coding of the currently selected step.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Button/state for the four Carnot steps: the learner clicks Next through M to N, N to O, O to P, and P to M, the active piston, heat arrow, work arrow, and reservoir or insulation block highlight, making clear the ordered expansion and compression processes in the cycle.
- Toggle between thermal contact and insulation: the learner selects isothermal or adiabatic steps, heat arrows appear only with the hot or cold reservoir and disappear inside insulation, making clear when energy crosses the boundary as heat.
- Toggle between piston panels and a p-V path view: the learner switches representations, the corresponding segment of the MNOP curve highlights as each cylinder state is selected, making clear how the physical piston motion maps to the thermodynamic cycle path.

With an ideal gas as the working substance, the steps of the Carnot cycle, as represented by the figure, are as follows.

The four processes of the Carnot cycle. The working substance is assumed to be an ideal gas whose thermodynamic path MNOP is represented in the figure.

discrepancies: Default (step-0) state is not a drop-in replacement for the source: panels 2–4 are rendered at 50% opacity and panel 1 carries an orange highlight ring, whereas the source shows all four panels at equal, full prominence.

Because the demo player starts on 'Step 1', the four-panel figure is never shown in its neutral form unless the user selects 'Full cycle' — the washed-out panels make W₂/W₃/W₄, 'Insulation', 'Reservoir' and '(Temperature T_c)' noticeably harder to read than in the source.
Text is rendered small relative to the inline size (780-unit viewbox squeezed into ~600 px), so caption/annotation type is smaller and lighter-weight than the source's fairly bold captions.
Q_h / Q_c labels sit closer to the 'Reservoir' text than in the source, producing a slightly crowded stack of labels at the bottom of the hot and cold panels.

Minor: the source's piston stem/slab and cylinder wall line weights are heavier and the cylinder wall is a distinct double-line; generated version uses a thinner single stroke, giving the cylinders a lighter appearance.
evaluation.notes: Structurally and conceptually faithful four-panel Carnot figure with correct colors, gas volumes, work/heat arrows and captions plus rich, working interactions (step player, step/boundary/view selectors, click popups, extra p–V view), but the default state dims three of the four panels and adds a highlight ring, and the overall type size is small, hurting the drop-in-replacement look and label legibility.
action_items: Make the initial state neutral: start with cycleStep = 'fullCycle' (no dimming, no orange ring) so the step-0 render matches the source, and only apply highlight/dimming once the user advances the demo or picks a step.
Raise the opacity floor for inactive panels (e.g. 0.75) or dim only the colored block fill while keeping text at full opacity, so W₂/W₃/W₄ and the block labels stay legible.
Increase base font sizes (or shrink the viewbox width) so captions render at ≥12 px inline, and give 'Step n:' headings and the W/Q symbols more weight to match the source's hierarchy.
Add a few pixels of separation between the Q_h/Q_c symbol and the 'Reservoir' label, matching the source's spacing, and thicken the cylinder wall stroke slightly.

plan.concept: The Carnot cycle consists of four ordered reversible processes — isothermal expansion in contact with a hot reservoir, adiabatic expansion under insulation, isothermal compression against a cold reservoir, and adiabatic compression under insulation — in which heat crosses the boundary only during the two isothermal steps while work is exchanged in all four.
elements: Four cylinder-and-piston panels arranged left to right, one per step of the cycle
Panel 1 surround: large red/salmon block labeled 'Reservoir' with sub-label '(Temperature T_h)'
Panel 2 surround: pale peach block labeled 'Insulation'
Panel 3 surround: blue block labeled 'Reservoir' with sub-label '(Temperature T_c)'
Panel 4 surround: pale peach block labeled 'Insulation'
Cylinder walls: open-topped gray-outlined rectangles, one per panel
Gas column in each cylinder: light gray fill stippled with small gray dots, height varying — medium (Step 1 start), tall (Step 2), tallest at start of Step 3 shrinking, shortest (Step 4 end)
Piston in each cylinder: pale lavender/blue slab sitting on top of the gas with a narrow vertical stem rising out of the cylinder mouth
Green work arrows: W1 upward (panel 1), W2 upward (panel 2), W3 downward (panel 3), W4 downward (panel 4), each with italic subscripted label
Thick gray heat arrows: Q_h pointing upward into the gas from the hot reservoir (panel 1), Q_c pointing downward out of the gas into the cold reservoir (panel 3); no heat arrow in panels 2 and 4
Bold captions beneath each panel: 'Step 1: Isothermal expansion (M→N)', 'Step 2: Adiabatic expansion (N→O)', 'Step 3: Isothermal compression (O→P)', 'Step 4: Adiabatic compression (P→M)'
Alternate view: p–V diagram with pressure axis (vertical, label 'p') and volume axis (horizontal, label 'V')
p–V closed loop with four labeled corner points M, N, O, P
p–V curve segments: M→N shallow isotherm at T_h, N→O steeper adiabat, O→P isotherm at T_c, P→M steeper adiabat, arrowheads showing clockwise traversal
p–V annotations: dashed isotherm guide curves labeled T_h and T_c, shaded loop interior labeled 'net work W'
Legend keying green = work, gray = heat, red = hot reservoir, blue = cold reservoir, peach = insulation

interactions.label: Carnot step
interactions.teaches: The cycle is an ordered sequence: gas expands hot, expands while insulated and cools, is compressed cold, then is compressed while insulated and reheats back to the starting state.

interactions.label: Show boundary condition
interactions.teaches: Heat crosses the cylinder wall only when the gas touches a reservoir; under insulation Q = 0 and the temperature must change instead.
interactions._note: Selecting a filter dims the non-matching panels and hides their heat arrows, making the Q-in / Q-out pairing explicit.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Each physical piston picture is one leg of the closed p-V loop; the highlighted panel and the highlighted curve segment are the same process seen two ways.

demo_steps.title: Step 1 — Isothermal expansion (M→N)
demo_steps.narration: The cylinder sits on the hot reservoir at T_h. Heat Q_h flows in (gray arrow up) exactly as fast as the gas does work W1 lifting the piston, so the temperature never changes and the gas expands.

demo_steps.title: Step 2 — Adiabatic expansion (N→O)
demo_steps.narration: The cylinder is now wrapped in insulation, so no heat arrow appears. The gas keeps expanding and does work W2, but that energy can only come from its own internal energy, so it cools from T_h to T_c.

demo_steps.title: Step 3 — Isothermal compression (O→P)
demo_steps.narration: Placed on the cold reservoir at T_c, the gas is compressed: work W3 is done on it downward while heat Q_c is dumped out to the cold reservoir, holding the temperature fixed.

demo_steps.title: Step 4 — Adiabatic compression (P→M)
demo_steps.narration: Insulated again, the gas is compressed to its smallest volume by work W4 with no heat exchange, which raises its temperature back to T_h and returns it to state M.

demo_steps.title: Where heat crosses the boundary
demo_steps.narration: Filter to the thermal-contact steps only: heat enters in Step 1 and leaves in Step 3. Every other energy transfer in the cycle is work, not heat.

demo_steps.title: Insulated legs change temperature, not heat
demo_steps.narration: Now filter to the insulated steps. With Q = 0, the work done goes entirely into or out of internal energy, which is what carries the gas between T_h and T_c.

demo_steps.title: The same cycle as a p-V loop
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the p-V view: the four panels become the four legs of a closed clockwise loop M→N→O→P→M. The shallow legs are isotherms, the steep legs adiabats, and the enclosed area is the net work output.

demo_steps.title: Linking picture to path
demo_steps.narration: Side by side, stepping through the cycle highlights one cylinder and its matching curve segment together, so piston motion, heat flow, and position on the loop are read as a single process.

plan.keyInsight: Heat enters only at T_h and leaves only at T_c; the two insulated legs exist purely to move the gas between those two temperatures without any heat crossing the boundary — which is why the closed loop encloses net work and why Carnot efficiency depends only on T_h and T_c.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Layout: four equal-width vertical panels in a row, each a tall colored surround block containing an open-topped gray-outlined cylinder. Surround colors left to right: saturated red (hot reservoir), pale peach (insulation), medium blue (cold reservoir), pale peach (insulation), each with its bold centered label near the bottom and reservoirs carrying an italic '(Temperature T_h)' / '(Temperature T_c)' line just below the block. Gas is a light-gray rectangle stippled with evenly scattered small dark-gray dots; the piston is a thin pale lavender slab with a narrow stem poking above the cylinder mouth. Gas column height grows across panels 1→2 (expansion) and shrinks across 3→4 (compression), shortest at the end of Step 4. Work arrows are thin green arrows beside the piston stem, pointing up in panels 1 and 2 and down in panels 3 and 4, labeled W1..W4 with italic subscripts. Heat arrows are thick gray arrows only in panels 1 (up, into gas, labeled Q_h) and 3 (down, out of gas, labeled Q_c). Bold two-line captions run beneath each panel with the step number, process name, and transition arrow (M→N etc.). Active step is shown by a bright outline / full opacity on its panel while others dim to ~35% opacity. The alternate p-V view is a clean line plot with p on the vertical axis and V on the horizontal, a clockwise closed quadrilateral-like loop with labeled corners M (upper left), N, O, P, shallow isothermal legs drawn in warm red (T_h) and cool blue (T_c), steep adiabatic legs in neutral dark gray, dashed extended isotherm guides labeled T_h and T_c, arrowheads mid-segment, and a lightly shaded interior labeled 'net work'. The highlighted segment matches the color coding of the currently selected step.

discrepancies: Heat arrows are considerably longer and thicker than in the source, and their heads/tails penetrate the cylinder wall (Q_h head at y=224 sits above the cylinder bottom at y=240; Q_c tail starts inside the gas) whereas in the source the gray arrow stops at / starts from the cylinder base.
The 'Reservoir' / 'Insulation' text sits flush against the bottom border of the coloured block, with much less clearance than the source, so the word nearly touches the rectangle outline.

The W-arrow labels (W₁, W₃, W₄) are pushed left of the arrow and overlap the white cylinder channel / cylinder wall stroke; in the source each W label sits clearly in the coloured region beside the arrow.

Panel proportions differ slightly: the source cylinders are narrower relative to the surrounding block and the piston rod is centred on the cylinder axis, while here the rod is offset to the right of centre.

Extra elements not in the source (p–V loop view with net-work shading, legend, corner labels M/N/O/P) are added — acceptable as hidden alternate views, but they are additions beyond the original figure.
evaluation.notes: Default view is an immediately recognisable reproduction of the four-panel Carnot figure with correct colours, gas volumes, arrows and full caption text, backed by a rich and genuinely pedagogical set of step/boundary/representation controls; main weaknesses are oversized heat arrows that intrude into the cylinder and a few tight label placements against block borders and cylinder walls.
action_items: Shorten the heat arrows so Q_h terminates at the cylinder base (y≈240) and Q_c starts at the base, matching the source's compact gray arrows, and reduce their stroke width slightly.
Raise the 'Reservoir'/'Insulation' labels ~8–10 px so they clear the bottom border of the coloured block, and add a little vertical margin above the '(Temperature T_h)' caption.
Shift the W arrow/label pair further left (or centre the piston rod) so the italic W subscript labels no longer overlap the white cylinder channel or its gray wall stroke.
Centre the piston stem on the cylinder axis as in the source and narrow the cylinder-to-block width ratio for closer proportional match.
